snippet.title: I powered my parents house with an EV battery!
snippet.description:
What happens when you take an EV battery out of a car… and install it at a house instead? ⚡🔋

In this video I install a large EV battery system at my parents’ house and connect it to a hybrid solar inverter to create a DIY home battery storage setup. The goal? Store cheap electricity, use more solar power, reduce grid costs, and explore whether repurposed electric vehicle batteries could become a realistic alternative to expensive commercial home battery systems.

This project uses real EV battery hardware, high voltage systems, battery communication, and inverter integration to turn a second-life car battery into a working home energy storage system.

Along the way I cover:
🔋 EV battery repurposing
⚡ Home battery storage
☀️ Solar inverter integration
🏠 DIY energy storage systems
🔧 High voltage battery installation
📈 Energy shifting and off-peak charging
🚗 Using EV batteries outside the car

As EVs become more common, huge numbers of used battery packs will eventually become available. Could these batteries power homes for years after leaving the road?

This video is part experiment, part engineering project, and part look into the future of home energy.

⚠️ Disclaimer:
This project involves dangerous high voltage systems and should not be attempted without suitable knowledge, training, and safety precautions.

snippet.title: Dealer Quoted £3,000 — I Fixed It for £380… But It Wouldn’t Work Until the Dealer Did THIS!
snippet.description:
If you own a Stellantis EV — Citroën, Peugeot, or Vauxhall — and your onboard charger has failed, this video is for you. I show exactly how I repaired and replaced a faulty EV onboard charger at home for a fraction of the dealer’s £3,000 quote. This works for many Stellantis models that share the same  OBC unit used across the entire range of electric vehicles between 2019 and 2025.

*** DISCLAIMER - Working with high voltage can be dangerous. While disconnecting the 12 V battery will stop the battery outputting power, if a component has failed in the battery,  power could still be output. Check the top left rear connector on the OBC to make sure that it doesn't have power and then test on your 12 V battery to confirm that your tester is working. A GS38 tester should be used or a multimeter for the DIYer. Keep safe. DISCLAIMER ***

In this video, I go step-by-step through the diagnosis, teardown, and repair process, showing what fails inside these chargers and how I got mine back on the road for just £380 — including the £130 dealer coding that no one else talks about!

You’ll see exactly what happens when you fit a replacement unit, why it won’t work without dealer coding, and what the coding process actually involves. I also share how to save time and money avoiding long dealership delays.

snippet.title: EV Batteries Are Becoming Unrepairable — And Honestly, It Makes Sense
snippet.description:
Sponsored by EnergieGenie.co.uk – Energie Genie is a smart software service that seamlessly integrates your renewable energy products: solar panels, home battery storage, and EV chargers for smarter, cheaper, automated energy use. 
Current offer for new customers, if they sign up and purchase our product via our website, they can try it for free for 3 months! (T's & C's apply)

EV batteries are changing — and so is the way they’re built.
In today’s video, I go deeper inside a Fisker Ocean battery pack to remove the  cells… and discover why modern EV battery modules are becoming unrepairable by design. And honestly? It makes complete sense.

This isn’t a hit piece on Fisker or the EV industry.
It’s a look at how manufacturing methods, cost reduction, thermal performance, and reliability all lead engineers toward sealed, highly integrated battery packs that simply aren’t meant to be taken apart after leaving the factory.

⸻

🔧 What You’ll See in This Video

• Attempting to remove a cell from a Fisker Ocean battery module
• Why the pack uses a tight ladder-frame construction
• How structural adhesives, potting, and thermal materials make service difficult
• The trade-offs between repairability, safety, and cost
• Why this design direction actually benefits EV owners

⸻

⚡ The Bigger Picture

A lot of EV battery debates focus on “right to repair,” but the reality is that manufacturers are prioritising reliability over modularity. When batteries last longer, fail less often, and are cheaper to produce, serviceability naturally becomes the compromise.

In 10 years, we’ll probably have a completely new approach to EV pack design. But right now, this is where the industry is — and this video shows you exactly why.
